title: How to cheat on LinkedIn to find jobs posted within the last 24 hours
description:
Trying to figure out how to find a job on LinkedIn quickly—but every role already has hundreds of applicants?

In this video, I break down how to find job leads posted on LinkedIn within the last hour.

Make sure to catch the full video below

https://youtu.be/h9MhKqPlzXs

where you will learn:

How to find jobs on LinkedIn posted in the last hour
How to use Boolean search to uncover current hiring activity
How to analyze recently hired candidates and position yourself in the same way
How to identify and connect with people in your target role
How to increase your visibility so you actually get seen

If LinkedIn has felt overwhelming or like you’re applying without hearing anything back, it’s not because you’re not qualified. It’s because you’re not being seen the way you should be, and that is fixable.

transcript: It is absolutely okay to cheat, especially when it comes to your job search. Check out this cool LinkedIn hack that helps you find jobs within the last 24 hours. Make sure to watch my full video on the LinkedIn cheat code, which is going to help you find jobs faster. I'm in the LinkedIn jobs tab and I typed in the title of the job I'm looking for, which is marketing manager. It's going to pull up a list of job leads, but here's the issue. It does not always pull up the newest post first. So, for example, this one was posted two days ago and then we go down already to a full month ago, which those jobs are going to be flooded with applications. So, we want to come up to the date posted and we want to click within the past 24 hours. This will show us more fresh results. Then we want to take this a step further and we come up here to our URL and we'll go all the way to the end and you'll see where it says TPR equals R86400. What this is is the amount of seconds in a 24-hour period. We want to change that to the number of seconds within the last hour. And that number happens to be 3,600. Go ahead and change that here. And this will bring up the leads that were posted most recently. Now, it still brings up that job lead that was posted 11 hours ago, but if you go down further, there's one that was 3 hours ago, one that was 7 hours ago, and here's one that was only an hour ago. Hopefully, when we click the past 24 hours, it does this already, bring up the most fresh postings, but sometimes it does not. So, if we click that 3,600 number, that is absolutely guaranteed to show us the newest postings and when we get on board fast, that can really make a difference.
